# Gruul Ramp

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Gruul Ramp: mana creatures into 5/5s, dragons and 8/8–12/8 monsters, with bite and burn removal; plays proactively and attacks every turn
- **Played by:** either. Suits whoever likes big creatures and straightforward attacking; the easier of the two to learn.
- **Status:** idea
- **Paired against:** [Izzet Prowess](izzet-prowess.md)
- **Complexity:** 2/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** Pair 2. It uses no precon cards, so its cards have all arrived and it can be built now. It's in **both** the Now set and the Commander-season set, so it only has to be taken apart if you build the Finneas Commander deck (6 shared cards; see Shared-pool conflicts).

A red-green ramp deck. Mana creatures on turns 1–2 let you cast 5/5s on turns 3–4, then 6/6 to 12/8 monsters and dragons. Your removal is 'bite' spells, where your big creature punches theirs, plus big burn. The plan is simple: cast the biggest creature you can and attack every turn. It's the easiest of the four decks to learn.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **2x Thragtusk** (replaces 2 Snakeskin Veil). A 5/3 that gains you 5 life when it enters and leaves a 3/3 behind when it leaves the battlefield (dies or is bounced), so it's great against burn and Into the Roil. It's also simpler for a beginner than timing Veil at instant speed, and it frees the Veils for another green deck. Sim +4.3 points. *Also useful in: Any green deck; a solid value creature for a green Commander deck (not an EDHREC staple for Halana and Alena or Ruby)..*
2. **2x Glorybringer** (replaces Tajuru Pathwarden + Savage Ventmaw). A 5-mana 4/4 flier with haste. When it attacks you may exert it to deal 4 damage to one of Izzet's non-Dragon creatures; it then skips your next untap, so it fires every other turn. Sprite Dragon and Firespitter Whelp are Dragons and can't be targeted, and Tolarian Terror's ward means paying 2 more. It's a Dragon, so it also triggers Lathliss. Sim +4.4 points. Izzet can still answer it with counters, Witness Protection, Charmed Sleep or a kicked Burst. *Also useful in: Lathliss, Dragon Queen Commander (in 16% of Lathliss decks on EDHREC); you already own Lathliss..*
3. **2x Rootbound Crag** (replaces 2 Rugged Highlands). An R/G dual that enters untapped when you control a Mountain or Forest, so the turn-1 elf into turn-2/3 four-drop works more often. Small in-matchup gain (lands together +1.7 points), but it's a permanent mana upgrade. *Also useful in: Halana and Alena (51% of decks on EDHREC) and Ruby, Daring Tracker (52%) Commander decks..*
4. **2x Cinder Glade** (replaces Gruul Guildgate + Temple of Abandon). A Mountain Forest dual that enters untapped once you control two basic lands, which is usually from turn 3. Because it's a Mountain and a Forest, it also turns on Rootbound Crag. *Also useful in: Halana and Alena (63% of decks on EDHREC) and Ruby (67%) Commander decks..*

### Shared-pool conflicts

Each physical card can only be in one deck at a time. These decks need some of the same copies:

- [Finneas, Ace Archer: Rabbits, Tokens and Counters](../commander/finneas-rabbits.md): 6 cards between the owned lists, 5 between the target lists. Druid of the Cowl, Eternal Witness, Garruk's Uprising, Rampaging Baloths, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Scavenging Ooze.

Shares no physical cards with: [Mono-White Angels](mono-white-angels.md), [Mono-Black Zombies](mono-black-zombies.md), [Izzet Prowess](izzet-prowess.md), [Selesnya Rabbits](selesnya-rabbits.md), [Orzhov Vampires](orzhov-vampires.md), [Mono-Black Midrange](mono-black-midrange.md), [Orzhov Removal Midrange](orzhov-removal.md), [Giada, Font of Hope: Calling All Angels (upgraded)](../commander/giada-angels.md), [Ghoulcaller Gisa: Wretched Ranks (upgraded)](../commander/gisa-zombies.md).

| 2 Thragtusk | 2 Snakeskin Veil | Veil (G, instant) saves your best creature from one burn spell, bounce or Heartfire's ability and gives it a +1/+1 counter, but you have to time it. Thragtusk's 5 life and 3/3 leftover are stronger against burn. About 4 points weaker. |
| 2 Rootbound Crag | 2 Rugged Highlands | Highlands enter tapped (you gain 1 life). About 1 point weaker. |
| 2 Cinder Glade | Gruul Guildgate + Temple of Abandon | Both enter tapped (Temple lets you scry 1). About 1 point weaker. |

## Notes

**Game plan.** You're the big-creature deck.
- On turns 1–2, play a mana creature (Llanowar Elves, Druid of the Cowl, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Ruby) so you have 4–5 mana on turn 3.
- Then play creatures bigger than anything Izzet has: 5/5s on turns 3–4, 6/6s to 12/8s after that. Attack every turn.
- Your removal is 'bite' spells (Bite Down, Rabid Gnaw: your creature deals damage equal to its power to their creature and doesn't get hit back) and burn (Flame Lash, Fiery Annihilation).
- Use removal on Izzet's damage engines and fliers: Guttersnipe, Coruscation Mage, Firespitter Whelp or Sprite Dragon, Mischievous Mystic and Bria.
- Tolarian Terror (5/5, ward 2) is hard to kill. Only Fiery Annihilation or a bite from a creature with 5+ power kills it (Flame Lash's 4 isn't enough), and you must pay 2 extra mana or your spell is countered.
- Izzet has no board wipe in its main deck, so you can keep adding creatures.

**Opening hand and mulligan.**
- Keep 7 cards with 2–5 lands. The dream hand is 3 lands, a mana creature and a 4–5 drop.
- Keep a 2-land hand only if it has a mana creature, and remember Izzet will try to burn that elf on turn 2.
- Mulligan hands with 0–1 lands, and hands that are all 6–7 drops with 2 lands and no mana creature.
- To mulligan, shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken. After one mulligan, keep 2–4 lands, or 1 land with 2 mana creatures.

**Play tips.**
1. **Sakura-Tribe Elder.** Block with it, then sacrifice it before damage to put a basic land onto the battlefield tapped: a free block plus extra mana. If Izzet points a burn spell at it, sacrifice it in response: you still get the land and their spell does nothing. If you don't need the block, sacrifice it at the end of Izzet's turn.
2. **Haste helpers.** At the start of each of your combats, Halana and Alena puts +1/+1 counters equal to its power (usually 2) on another of your creatures and gives it haste. Cast your new creature *before* combat so it can attack straight away. Surrak does a similar haste trick once your creatures' total power is 8 or more.
3. **Bite with your biggest creature.** Gnarlback Rhino draws you a card whenever you cast a spell that targets it (Bite Down, Rabid Gnaw, Snakeskin Veil).
4. **Bait the counterspell.** If Izzet leaves two blue mana open, they may have Counterspell. Cast your second-best creature first to draw it out, then your best one.
5. **Scavenging Ooze.** Spend spare green mana exiling cards from graveyards. Creature cards make the Ooze bigger and gain you life. Exiling Izzet's instants and sorceries makes Tolarian Terror and Enigma Drake weaker and stops Think Twice's flashback.
6. **Garruk's Uprising.** Cast it before your big creatures: you draw a card for each creature with power 4 or more that enters afterwards.
7. **Terror of Mount Velus.** The turn it enters, all your creatures get double strike, so cast it before combat and attack with everything else.
8. **Wildheart Invoker.** Late game, {8} gives your best attacker +5/+5 and trample for the turn.

**Watch out for (Izzet).**
- Counterspell (counters anything) and Essence Scatter (creatures only), when Izzet has 1–2 blue mana open.
- Witness Protection turns your best creature into a 1/1 with no abilities. Charmed Sleep keeps it tapped, but its other abilities (Baloths' landfall, Halana's counters) still work.
- Into the Roil returns your creature to your hand, and tokens simply vanish.
- Guttersnipe (2 damage per instant or sorcery) and Coruscation Mage (1 per noncreature spell) hurt you every time Izzet casts a spell. Kill them first.
- Heartfire Immolator can sacrifice itself to deal its power in damage to one of your creatures, even in response to your removal. Snakeskin Veil (owned list) can stop that ability.
- Bria gives all of Izzet's creatures prowess, and every noncreature spell makes one of them unblockable that turn.
- In the upgraded Izzet: Sprite Dragon grows permanently (kill it early; it's a Dragon, so Glorybringer can't target it), and Electrolyze can kill two elves at once.

**Sideboard: only against stronger opponents, never against Izzet.**
- The cards:
  - Chaos Warp answers any permanent, including enchantments, planeswalkers and indestructible creatures.
  - Broken Wings destroys a flier, artifact or enchantment (great against Angels).
  - Skyraker Giant is a 4/3 blocker with reach.
  - Incinerating Blast deals 6 damage to a creature.
  - Flame Lash #3.
  - Obliterating Bolt deals 4 damage to a creature and exiles it if it would die, so it can't come back (good against Zombies).
- Against fliers: bring in Broken Wings and Skyraker Giant. Take out 2 Snakeskin Veil (owned list), or Clifftop Lookout and Fierce Empath (upgraded list).
- Against big creatures or enchantments: bring in Chaos Warp, Incinerating Blast and Flame Lash. Take out Clifftop Lookout, Fierce Empath and Gnarlback Rhino.
- Against creature swarms or graveyard decks: bring in Obliterating Bolt. Take out Wildheart Invoker.

### Head-to-head vs Izzet Prowess (tested)

**Verdict: even**, about 51/49 Izzet with competent play on both sides. If the Izzet player is still learning, it's closer to 49/51.

| Izzet win % | Original simulator | Re-checked simulator |
|---|---|---|
| Owned vs owned | 51–53% | 51% (49% with beginner-level Izzet play) |
| Both with buys | 51–53% | 51% (49% with beginner-level Izzet play) |
| Izzet with buys, Gruul owned | 60% | 59% |
| Izzet owned, Gruul with buys | 41% | 42% |

**How it was tested.** A rules simulator played 32,000 games per matchup, alternating who goes first. An independent re-check found a bug worth about 2 points to Izzet (Gruul never sacrificed Sakura-Tribe Elder in response to burn) and five smaller gaps. It fixed them all, then restored the balance with one list change: Gruul's Obliterating Bolt moved to the sideboard and Wildheart Invoker came in. Twelve simulator games were also reviewed turn by turn (6–6), and 8 more were played by hand. Gruul won 6 of those 8, but the simulator also favoured Gruul on the same deals (Izzet won 41%).

**Going first is the biggest single factor.** Izzet wins about 55% on the play and 47% on the draw. Take turns going first, or let Izzet start if Gruul keeps winning.

#### Why it's even
- The red cards are split. Izzet has all the cheap burn and the prowess creatures. Gruul has the big burn, the bite spells and the red giants.
- Izzet's burn kills Gruul's mana creatures but not its giants. For those it has counterspells, Witness Protection, Charmed Sleep, Into the Roil, kicked Burst Lightning and double burn. Gruul's 7 main-deck removal spells kill any Izzet creature except Tolarian Terror.
- **Gruul wins** when a mana creature survives or it lands a 6-drop that Izzet can't answer. **Izzet wins** when it kills the early elves and races with flyers and pings. Izzet's results depend more on how well it's played.

#### Buying rule
Izzet's buys are worth about +8 points and Gruul's about +9, so upgrade both decks together. Otherwise buy the threats first for both (Sprite Dragon ×3 with Glorybringer ×2, tested at 51%), not the lands first (about 53% Izzet). On 2026-09-28 MTGMate had no Glorybringer or Electrolyze, so find those at Good Games or the local shop. Keep both decks on their owned lists until both packages are complete, then swap them in on the same day.

#### Tuning levers (measured in the re-checked simulator)
- **If Gruul wins too often:** let Izzet go first (see above). Card swaps help Izzet only a little: Gruul's Fiery Annihilation → Beast-Kin Ranger is +0.3 to +0.7 for Izzet.
- **If Izzet wins too often:** Gruul's Wildheart Invoker → Obliterating Bolt from its sideboard (−2 to −3 for Izzet), or Gruul's Fierce Empath → Giant Cindermaw (about −1.5).
- **If Izzet feels too complicated:** cut to 1 Counterspell and add Opt (about −0.6 for Izzet), and let Izzet go first.
- **Not levers:** Izzet's Mischievous Mystic → Charmed Sleep (−0.6 for Izzet, the wrong direction). Gruul's Garruk's Uprising → Harmonize won't work either: Harmonize is in the Selesnya Rabbits sideboard, so both decks couldn't be built in the Commander-season set.
- Most single-card swaps move the result by less than 1 point, so log about 10 real games before changing anything.

Simulator code and full game logs from the 2026-09-28 analysis are not kept in the repo.
